title: Chicken and rice casserole
subtitle: Classic American baked chicken thighs over seasoned rice
excerpt: Chicken thighs baked over long-grain rice in seasoned chicken stock with onion, garlic, and herbs until the rice has absorbed all the liquid and the chicken skin is golden. The great one-pan American casserole.
sourceNotes: Chicken and rice casserole is a fixture of American church-supper and community cookbook cooking, documented from the early twentieth century. It appears in Joy of Cooking and in every major American community cookbook from the mid-twentieth century. The combination of bone-in chicken baked over uncooked rice, which absorbs the cooking liquid, is a distinctly American technique.

recipe.makeAheadNotes: Assemble without baking up to 6 hours ahead. Bake just before serving.

content.text: Chicken and rice casserole is one of the most practical dishes in this collection: everything goes into one tin, the oven does the work, and the rice absorbs all the cooking juices and becomes full of chicken flavour. The ratio of stock to rice is precise. Too little and the rice is chalky; too much and it is wet. Stick to the quantities.
Heat the oven to 190°C (fan 170°C). Mix the rinsed rice, onion, garlic, and thyme together in a large baking dish. Pour over the stock. Stir to combine. Taste the liquid and season with salt.

Pat the chicken thighs dry and season with salt, pepper, smoked paprika, and garlic powder. Rub with the oil. Place skin-side up on top of the rice, pushing them down slightly so they are half-submerged in the liquid.

Cover tightly with foil and bake for 30 minutes. Remove the foil and bake for a further 30 to 35 minutes until the chicken skin is golden and crisp and the rice has absorbed all the liquid. Rest for 10 minutes before serving.

items.symptom: Rice is undercooked or still firm
items.cause: Liquid was too hot when it went in, or oven temperature was too high (liquid evaporated rather than absorbed)
items.fix: Add an extra 100 ml of hot water, cover, and return to the oven for 10 more minutes.
Next time, reduce the stock to 700 ml for 400 g rice.

content.text: Chicken and rice casserole is church-supper America: practical, generous, and entirely reliable. It appears in virtually every Southern and Midwestern American community cookbook. The names vary. Sometimes it is called chicken bog; sometimes pilau, which reflects its South Carolina and lowcountry roots. At its simplest it is a weeknight family dinner. At its most celebrated it is Carolina pilau, with smoke and seafood.
